title: explicit
description:
A constructor with one parameter also works as a silent converter: with `Metres(double)`, a function expecting `Metres` happily accepts a bare `5.0`. That is rarely what you want.

Write a class `Metres` whose single-argument constructor is marked `explicit`, plus `double value() const`.

The tests check that `Metres{ 5.0 }` works and that a `double` does **not** convert to `Metres` on its own.
hints: Write `explicit` in front of the constructor: `explicit Metres(double value) : m_value{ value } {}`. Nothing else changes; the tests then check that a plain `double` is refused.
